subject: Career
title: How ATS Software Works
description: A short lesson to help you apply How ATS Software Works.

hook.text: 75% of resumes are rejected before a human sees them. The gatekeeper is software.

buildup.text: Applicant Tracking Systems parse your resume, extract keywords, and rank you against others.

discovery.text: They look for exact keyword matches. 'Project management' and 'managed projects' may score differently.

twist.text: Fancy formatting, tables, and graphics often break ATS parsing entirely.

climax.text: The irony: the resume that impresses humans might be invisible to machines.

punchline.text: Get past the robot first. Impress the human second.

quiz.question: What percentage of resumes are rejected before a human reviews them?

details.summary: Applicant tracking systems parse resumes into structured data fields, search for keyword matches against job descriptions, and rank candidates by relevance score. Understanding this automated first filter is essential because most resumes are rejected by software before a human sees them.
details.whyItMatters: Up to seventy-five percent of resumes are filtered out by ATS before reaching a recruiter. A well-qualified candidate with a poorly formatted resume can be eliminated by an algorithm.
takeaways: ATS parses your resume into structured fields like education and experience
Keyword matching compares your content against the job description
Simple formatting ensures accurate parsing of your information

faq.question: How do applicant tracking systems rank candidates after parsing resumes?
faq.answer: ATS assigns relevance scores based on keyword matches with the job description, recency of relevant experience, job title alignment, and sometimes skills proficiency levels. Higher-scoring resumes appear at the top of the recruiter's queue, dramatically increasing review probability.

faq.question: Do all companies use applicant tracking systems in their hiring process?
faq.answer: Over ninety percent of large companies and about seventy percent of mid-size companies use some form of ATS. Small companies and startups may review resumes manually. When applying through online portals, assume an ATS is involved and optimize accordingly.
